judge: Two judges, each a Claude agent shown only the match sheet's claims and truth, not which method made the claims, ruled on every claim without seeing each other's rulings. An adjudicating agent ruled on each claim where they differed. Rules: the same problem at the same place; a general claim states nothing; when unsure, no match.

matches.note: The code summary says 6 stories and the set shows 5 floors.
Allowable stories under Table 504.4 for Type IIIA. This is a different defect from 6 declared vs 5 drawn, and it is not a stair count.
The index lists A7.1 Roof Plan, and no such sheet is in the set.

One stair serving 5 stories, short of the two exits required and over the single-exit allowances for stories. This says every story is short, including the fourth and fifth floors. Not matched to check 11 on THIRD FLOOR: that item comes from the stair being erased on the third floor, and this claim treats the stair as present on all five stories.
What the exit enclosure contains. No truth item covers this.
Same G1.3 stair marker giving 46 people, flagged as too small for the load. The claim gives the load as 52 and the truth gives 65, but the defect is the same.
Fire-resistance ratings not shown. No truth item covers this.
The A1.2 title block says Third Floor Plan and the drawing label says Second Floor Plan.
Room 202 on A1.2 is labeled Office where Bedroom is expected: same room and same Office/Bedroom conflict. The claim compares against other floors, not the finish schedule.
Window sill height and fall protection. No truth item covers this.
General EERO request for bedrooms on A1.1. It does not say the stair is missing on the first floor.
